title.narrative: Strengthened tripartite capacity to improve labour migration governance and address child labour in Eswatini

description.narrative: Some of the critical issues Eswatini’s recently adopted National Labour Migration Policy seeks to address is to strengthen the governance of labour migration to protect the rights of workers, and to strengthen the portability of migrants’ social security benefits. The ILO’s CEARC has also expressed concerns regarding gaps in Eswatini’s implementation of ratified Child Labour Conventions. The CEARC has also urged Government to take the necessary steps to make education compulsory (and not only free) for students at the primary and lower secondary levels, up until the minimum age for admission to employment (15 years); and to expedite the adoption of the Employment bill that seeks to address most of the concerns raised by the CEARC regarding child labour. The existing National Action Programme for Combating Child Labour (2021-2026) is also not well aligned with the Durban Call to Action towards the elimination of child labour; and the intersectoral committee established to drive and oversee its implementation does not have adequate capacity. A national wellness policy that seeks to provide inclusive HIV/AIDS and Wellness services is still to be adopted by Cabinet. The Strategy will focus on capacity and advisory support towards the operationalization of the National Labour Migration Policy and its accompanying action plan, paying particular attention to reviewing institutional arrangements for its implementation; gap analyses for migration related Conventions C97 and C143, and strengthening mechanisms for the portability of migrants’ social security benefits in line with the SADC guidelines for the portability of migrants’ benefits.
